name: chest x-ray overview
title: Reading a chest X-ray with DRS. ABCDE so no zone is skipped, then telling the common abnormalities apart: white where air should be (airspace disease, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, collapse, with the midline pushed away by an effusion and pulled toward a collapse), black where lung should be (pneumothorax, tension if the trachea deviates), and lines or spots (interstitial lung disease, nodules and masses)

root.title: Chest X-ray (CXR): read it the SAME WAY every time, DRS. ABCDE, so nothing is missed
lines: Details · RIPE: Rotation (clavicle ends equidistant), Inspiration (anterior ribs 5–6 or posterior 8–10), Picture, Exposure
Soft tissue, bones · Airway, mediastinum: TRACHEA deviated? · Breathing: PNEUMOTHORAX?
Circulation: heart size on a back-to-front (PA) film; a portable front-to-back film magnifies it
Diaphragm: FREE AIR? (see the ACUTE ABDOMEN chart) · Extras: tubes, lines, devices · compare with OLD films
